transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you in today?

Um… yeah. I’m sorry, I’m not really sure how to explain it without sounding… odd. My wife wanted me to come in because I’ve been hearing things in the house—like water running, or men whispering in the walls—when nobody’s there.

I know that probably sounds strange. I check, and there’s nothing. And sometimes I’ll think I see this dark, wet-looking patch spreading across the hallway, but when I go look, it’s dry. My wife got pretty scared by it, so… that’s why I’m here.
Have you been feeling unusually down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or on the flip side, have you been feeling unusually energetic, restless, or overly confident lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I have been pretty down. Most days I wake up already feeling like I’ve failed somehow… as a husband, as a man, I guess. And that heaviness just kind of stays with me all day until I go to bed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with friends or family?

Yeah… I guess I have. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just being lazy or anything.

I used to be the kind of guy who showed up for soccer, brewed beer out in the garage, helped out at the fire department… stuff like that mattered to me. Lately it all just feels kind of pointless. I can’t really make myself care enough to go, even when I know I probably should.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt more confident than usual—so much so that it was noticeable to others or led to risky behavior?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had days where I tried to push through or act more normal, maybe got a little restless, but not like… staying up all night full of energy or feeling like I could do anything.

At least, not that anyone’s pointed out to me. My wife would probably notice, I think. Is that what you mean?
Have you found that things that used to bring you pleasure, like time with friends or your hobbies, just don’t feel good anymore?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve given up on everything, but… the things that used to feel good just don’t really land anymore.

Like soccer, or brewing beer in the garage, helping at the fire department—those used to make me feel like myself. Now I just look at them and think, what’s the point, you know? I can’t seem to make myself care enough to go. Is that… what you’re asking?

Have you experienced any other strange things that aren’t happening in reality—like seeing, hearing, or feeling things that others wouldn’t, or having unusual thoughts that others might not understand?

Um… yeah. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but… there have been some things.

What finally really scared my wife is I keep hearing water running, like in the walls, and sometimes men whispering in there too. I’ll check and there’s nobody there, no leak or anything.

And sometimes I see this dark, wet-looking patch spreading across the hallway floor… but when I go look, it’s dry. I know that probably sounds strange. I’m not trying to be difficult or dramatic. That’s just… what’s been happening.

When you hear the whispers or see the dark patches, do they ever say or represent something that fits with the way you’ve been feeling, like telling you that you’ve failed or don’t matter, or do they seem unrelated to how you’re feeling?

I’m not sure they’re saying anything that clear… not like a sentence about me, if that makes sense.

The water sound and the whispering in the walls — it’s more like I can’t make out what the men are saying. It feels… connected somehow, because it happens when I’m already feeling low or worked up, but I don’t know if it’s actually “about” me.

And the dark wet patch in the hallway… I guess it just feels bad, like something’s wrong, but I don’t look at it and think it means one specific thing. Sorry, I don’t know if that answers it right.

When you experience the sounds or see the dark patch, do they ever seem to match how you're feeling inside—like they're part of the same sadness or guilt—or do they feel more like something separate, just happening at the same time?

I think… more separate, maybe. I mean, it happens when I’m already not doing great, so it feels like it goes along with it in some way, but it’s not like the whispers are clearly saying I’m guilty or anything like that.

It’s just… the water running in the walls, or men whispering where nobody is, and then that dark wet-looking patch in the hallway even after I check and it’s dry. It scares me, but I don’t know that it “means” something about how I feel. Does that make sense?

When you hear the whispers or see the dark patch, do they ever feel like they’re directly related to your sadness, guilt, or low mood—like they’re reinforcing those feelings—or do they feel completely unrelated to what you’re thinking or feeling inside?

I think… not directly, no. I mean, I’m already in a bad place when it happens, so maybe it makes everything feel worse, but the whispers aren’t saying, like, “you failed” or anything I can make out.

It’s more just… the water running in the walls, and men whispering in there when nobody’s there. And the dark wet-looking patch in the hallway, even after I check and it’s dry. It feels frightening and wrong, but I don’t know that it’s tied to my sadness exactly. Is that… is that what you mean?

Have the things you hear or see ever seemed to directly reflect or match the thoughts you have about yourself, like confirming that you’ve failed or don’t matter, or do they feel more like something strange that’s just happening, without clearly connecting to your thoughts about yourself?

I don’t think they match my thoughts that directly, no. It’s not like the men whispering in the walls are saying I don’t matter or that I failed… at least I can’t make out anything like that.

It feels more like something strange happening, I guess. The water running, the whispering when nobody’s there, and sometimes that dark wet patch in the hallway even after I’ve checked and it’s dry. It scares me, and I know my wife got really worried about it, but I can’t say it’s clearly connected to what I think about myself. Does that answer what you’re asking?

Have you ever doubted that these things you’re hearing or seeing—like the water running, the whispers, or the dark patch—are actually happening, or do you feel certain they’re real even when others don’t experience them?

I… I try to doubt it, if that makes sense. I’ll tell myself it’s probably nothing, or maybe I’m just tired. But in the moment it feels real.

Like the water running in the walls—I can hear it, and sometimes the men whispering too, even when nobody’s there. And with the hallway, I’ve checked it, and it’s dry, but then I still see that dark wet-looking patch spreading there. That’s the part that really scared my wife.

I know other people don’t see it or hear it, so I don’t want to sound… I don’t know, dramatic. But when it’s happening, it doesn’t feel imagined. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have there been times when you weren’t sure whether these experiences—like the water running or the dark patch—were really happening or if it was just in your head?

Yes… there have been times I wasn’t sure. I’ll check, especially with the hallway, and it’s dry, so I know that should settle it. But then I still see this dark, wet-looking patch spreading, and in that moment it feels like it’s really there.

Same with the water running in the walls, and the men whispering… I know nobody else is there, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I hear it. That’s what finally really scared my wife, I think. I guess I go back and forth between telling myself it’s in my head and feeling like it’s actually happening. Does that make sense?

Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others around you didn’t believe, even when they had evidence against it—like thinking something is trying to harm you or that you have special abilities others don’t?

I mean… I wouldn’t say special abilities or anything like that. Nothing like that.

But there is something I’ve been worried about, and I know it probably sounds far-fetched. The house we were in… I’m pretty certain the mold and the wiring somehow poisoned everything I own. Clothes, furniture, boxes—just everything feels contaminated from it.

And I can tell the neighbors are watching, too. Like they’re waiting to see when I mess up again. I know that probably doesn’t sound reasonable when I say it out loud, but it feels very real to me. Does that make sense, or am I answering it wrong?

How do you feel when others tell you that the house isn't contaminated or that the neighbors aren't watching you? Do you find yourself still completely sure that you're right, even if no one else sees it that way?

I try not to argue with people about it, because I know how it sounds. I don’t want to seem unreasonable.

But… honestly, yes, even when they say the house isn’t contaminated, I still feel pretty certain it is. The mold and the wiring in that house, it feels like they poisoned everything I own—my clothes, the furniture, boxes, all of it. People tell me that can’t be right, and I nod along, but inside I don’t really believe them.

And with the neighbors… I know maybe I shouldn’t say I “know,” but it feels like I can tell they’re watching, waiting to see when I mess up again. I wish I didn’t feel so sure about it. Does that answer what you mean?

Do the things you believe about the house being contaminated and the neighbors watching feel like they’re connected to the sadness and guilt you’ve been feeling, or do they seem like something separate from how you’ve been feeling inside?

I think they’re connected… at least, that’s how it seems to me.

Before all the problems with the house dragged on, and before I got this low, I wasn’t hearing things in the walls or seeing wet spots that weren’t really there. And I didn’t used to think the neighbors were keeping track of me or waiting for me to mess up.

It was after I’d already kind of stopped caring about normal things and started feeling like I was failing every day that all of that started. So… I don’t know if I’m explaining it right, but it doesn’t feel totally separate from the sadness and guilt. It feels like it came out of that somehow.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the heard sounds and seen dark patch are perceived as real despite others not experiencing them, which most directly concerns hallucinations.

patient.answer:
I… I try to doubt it, if that makes sense. I’ll tell myself it’s probably nothing, or maybe I’m just tired. But in the moment it feels real.

Like the water running in the walls—I can hear it, and sometimes the men whispering too, even when nobody’s there. And with the hallway, I’ve checked it, and it’s dry, but then I still see that dark wet-looking patch spreading there. That’s the part that really scared my wife.

I know other people don’t see it or hear it, so I don’t want to sound… I don’t know, dramatic. But when it’s happening, it doesn’t feel imagined. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has experienced a loss of insight into the unreality of his perceptual experiences, which would support a diagnosis of major depressive disorder with psychotic features (F32.3) over adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.22).
doctor.question: Have there been times when you weren’t sure whether these experiences—like the water running or the dark patch—were really happening or if it was just in your head?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: What finally scared my wife is that I keep hearing water running and men whispering inside the walls when nobody’s there, and sometimes I see a dark wet patch spreading across the hallway even after I’ve checked and it’s dry.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the patient doubts the reality of hearing water, whispers, or seeing the dark patch, which directly concerns hallucination-like perceptual experiences.

patient.answer:
Yes… there have been times I wasn’t sure. I’ll check, especially with the hallway, and it’s dry, so I know that should settle it. But then I still see this dark, wet-looking patch spreading, and in that moment it feels like it’s really there.

Same with the water running in the walls, and the men whispering… I know nobody else is there, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I hear it. That’s what finally really scared my wife, I think. I guess I go back and forth between telling myself it’s in my head and feeling like it’s actually happening. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a major depressive episode with psychotic features or a schizophrenia spectrum disorder, based on the presence and nature of delusions or hallucinations.
doctor.question: Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others around you didn’t believe, even when they had evidence against it—like thinking something is trying to harm you or that you have special abilities others don’t?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds far-fetched, but I’m certain the mold and wiring in that house have poisoned everything I own, and I can tell the neighbors are watching to see when I mess up again.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about strongly held beliefs that others do not share and that persist despite contrary evidence, such as beliefs about being harmed, which directly matches delusions.

patient.answer:
I mean… I wouldn’t say special abilities or anything like that. Nothing like that.

But there is something I’ve been worried about, and I know it probably sounds far-fetched. The house we were in… I’m pretty certain the mold and the wiring somehow poisoned everything I own. Clothes, furniture, boxes—just everything feels contaminated from it.

And I can tell the neighbors are watching, too. Like they’re waiting to see when I mess up again. I know that probably doesn’t sound reasonable when I say it out loud, but it feels very real to me. Does that make sense, or am I answering it wrong?

inference.note: The patient described persistent low mood, anhedonia, and feelings of failure, supporting a major depressive episode (F32.3). Additionally, the patient endorsed auditory and visual perceptual disturbances (e.g., hearing water running and whispers, seeing dark patches) that occur in the context of depressed mood but are not clearly mood-congruent or mood-incongruent delusions. There was no clear evidence of delusions or formal thought disorder to support a primary psychotic disorder. The patient also described concerns about environmental contamination and being watched, which may be mood-congruent or represent paranoid ideation, but not fixed delusions. Further questioning would be needed to clarify whether these experiences meet criteria for psychotic features in the context of depression or a separate psychotic disorder.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's delusional beliefs (e.g., about contamination or being watched) are fixed and unshakable despite evidence to the contrary, which would support a major depressive disorder with psychotic features (F23.9) over a non-psychotic severe depressive episode (F32.3).
doctor.question: How do you feel when others tell you that the house isn't contaminated or that the neighbors aren't watching you? Do you find yourself still completely sure that you're right, even if no one else sees it that way?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds far-fetched, but I’m certain the mold and wiring in that house have poisoned everything I own, and I can tell the neighbors are watching to see when I mess up again.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient remains certain about beliefs that others dispute, specifically contamination and neighbors watching, which directly assesses fixed delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
I try not to argue with people about it, because I know how it sounds. I don’t want to seem unreasonable.

But… honestly, yes, even when they say the house isn’t contaminated, I still feel pretty certain it is. The mold and the wiring in that house, it feels like they poisoned everything I own—my clothes, the furniture, boxes, all of it. People tell me that can’t be right, and I nod along, but inside I don’t really believe them.

And with the neighbors… I know maybe I shouldn’t say I “know,” but it feels like I can tell they’re watching, waiting to see when I mess up again. I wish I didn’t feel so sure about it. Does that answer what you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's delusional beliefs are mood-congruent or mood-incongruent, to differentiate between F23.9 (Delusional Disorder) and F32.3 (Major Depressive Disorder, Recurrent, With Psychotic Features).
doctor.question: Do the things you believe about the house being contaminated and the neighbors watching feel like they’re connected to the sadness and guilt you’ve been feeling, or do they seem like something separate from how you’ve been feeling inside?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Before the house problems dragged on and I fell into this depression, I never heard voices in the walls, saw wet patches that weren’t there, or thought the neighbors were tracking me. Those things only showed up after I had already stopped caring about my usual life and started feeling like a failure every day.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the beliefs about contamination and being watched are tied to the depressive sadness and guilt rather than being separate, which most directly relates to psychotic symptoms occurring in connection with the major depressive episode.

patient.answer:
I think they’re connected… at least, that’s how it seems to me.

Before all the problems with the house dragged on, and before I got this low, I wasn’t hearing things in the walls or seeing wet spots that weren’t really there. And I didn’t used to think the neighbors were keeping track of me or waiting for me to mess up.

It was after I’d already kind of stopped caring about normal things and started feeling like I was failing every day that all of that started. So… I don’t know if I’m explaining it right, but it doesn’t feel totally separate from the sadness and guilt. It feels like it came out of that somehow.

inference.note: The patient's delusions (house contamination, neighbors watching) and hallucinations (whispers, dark patches) appear mood-congruent and developed in the context of a major depressive episode. There is no evidence of manic symptoms ruling out bipolar disorder (F31.x). The psychotic features are better explained by major depressive disorder with psychotic features rather than a primary psychotic disorder (F23.9) due to their mood congruence and temporal relationship to the depression.
